niche: a 300 mm fab's sort-yield edge ring traced to the CMP conditioner disk, its cost counted at wafer sort and at package burn-in, its dose read on the supplier lot the units draw from stores, and the disk's own change count set at the cost optimum
answer: take the conditioner disk out of the full PM under Rev G and change it after 1,010 wafers of its own use on PU-1 and PU-2 and 840 on PU-3 and PU-4, saving about USD 519,000 a year against Rev F
analyst_test: The careful but hurried review rebuilds every counter, fits the outer zone's excess on a hinge in each pair's disk use with every rival beside it and measures the ring against the fallout on young disks, then fits each pair over every disk it ran, takes final test's burn-in failures in proportion to the ring's die at sort, sets the count on that curve and that proportion and prices Rev F on the same curve, so the counts run long and the saving is understated.
domain_test: Attributing a yield loss across correlated process features to the mechanism that carries it, reading that mechanism's dose on the supplier cohort a serial range names, and modelling its latent second-stage failures from lot totals on each lot's own wafers is the interpretability statistician's work; with a hospital's wards in place of tools, the serial ranges, the burn-in stage and the die-zone null stop making sense.

driver: The decisive quantities are a part's dose-response read on the supplier cohort the units will run, which only a typed serial and a receipt's serial range name, and a latent second-stage loss the downstream test reports only in batch totals, modelled on each batch's own units with its own onset and level; read off every cohort pooled and with the second stage taken in proportion to the first, the replacement count runs long and the saving is understated.
driver_concrete: Tessaline's Fab 2 edge ring: the sort-yield loss since April measured on each wafer's outer band against its interior and the fallout on young disks, traced to the CMP conditioner disk; the disks stores issue now are a supplier lot whose wear starts the ring 28 to 38 per cent sooner, named only by the serials the PM log typed and the receipts' serial ranges; and thinned edge dielectric fails burn-in at final test from about half the ring's onset, seen only in lot totals, so the disk's own count is set on the current lot's curve with both stages of loss.
stump: The careful but hurried review fits each pair's curve over every disk lot (onsets 1,540 and 850 against 840 and 640 on the lot in stores), takes final test's burn-in in proportion to the ring's die at sort (29,300 units against 114,900), sets the counts on that curve and that proportion (1,730 and 1,170 against 1,010 and 840) and prices Rev F on the same curve (USD 274,000 a year against 519,000), while its loss at sort and its causes land inside their bands.
results: R1 the ring's loss at sort on wafers sorted 1 April to 31 August, in points of mean wafer sort yield and good die by product; R2 each candidate cause's share (the conditioner disk's wear, the pad's life on top of it, the retaining ring, DEP-3, SC-4, the chambers' RF hours); R3 the units final test lost to the ring on lots it finished 1 April to 31 August, by product; R4 each unit's onset and climb on the disks it will be fitted with from September (the supplier lot in stores); R5 each unit's count for the disk once Rev G takes it out of the full PM, the ring costed at sort and at final test (the call); R6 the yearly saving against Rev F as it stands
